title: nntp: Path: header not updated on article transit (son-of-1036 violation)
description:
Why: RFC 1036 / son-of-1036 requires each transit node to prepend its own hostname to the Path: header when forwarding an article. The NNTP reader and transit session handlers never read or modify the Path: header. Without this, loop detection (duplicate Path: entry check) is impossible and the article path is invisible to downstream peers.

What: In the transit IHAVE/TAKETHIS ingestion path, before storing the article:
  1. Parse the existing Path: header value (or create it if absent).
  2. Check whether config.hostname already appears — if so, reject as a loop.
  3. Prepend config.hostname to the Path: value and rewrite the header.
The reader POST path should also prepend the reader's hostname when injecting an article.
